question: For each candidate Stage 3 domain, which of its central questions are identifiable from typed binary relational structure, and which are provably not?
why_first: P-21 and P-22 together. Before choosing a domain, rule out the ones where the distinction they care about is absent from the representation. A witness pair proves impossibility in an afternoon and saves committing to a domain that cannot work. Stage 2 was closed partly because this screen was never run on it.
soundness_is_one_directional: A witness pair PROVES a question is not identifiable. Failing to construct one proves nothing — it may mean I did not think of the right pair. So this screen rules domains OUT and can never rule one IN. Every 'identifiable' verdict below means only 'not ruled out here'.
the_bias_i_control_and_cannot_remove: I am choosing both the domains' central questions AND the witness pairs. Two degrees of freedom, both mine. A domain could be exonerated because I picked a question it happens to handle, or condemned because I picked an unrepresentative one. This is stated because it cannot be engineered away without a practitioner from each domain, which the project does not have.
method: For each (domain, question) pair: construct two cases that a practitioner would need DIFFERENT answers for, encode both as typed directed structures under the current representation, and test isomorphism exhaustively. Isomorphic + different answers required = not identifiable.
statistic: per (domain, question): identifiable / not identifiable, plus the channel that would be required to fix it
tests: exhaustive bijection search over node relabellings, including normalised relation weights (the magnitude channel added in EXP-034). No statistics -- these are proofs or they are nothing.
exclusion_rule: none. Every constructed pair is reported, including pairs that fail to be isomorphic, because a failed refutation is informative about what the representation DOES carry.
robustness: each domain gets at least two questions -- one expected to pass and one expected to fail -- so a domain reported as wholly viable or wholly dead is visibly the result of the questions chosen rather than of the screen being unable to discriminate.
falsification: every question in every domain comes back identifiable -> the screen has no discriminating power as built, probably because my witness pairs are too weak. Report as a failed screen, not as good news.
every question comes back not-identifiable -> the representation is narrower than EXP-048 suggests and Stage 3 has no viable domain on this list.
a mix -> the useful outcome: a map of which QUESTIONS are viable, which is finer-grained than which domains are.

predictions.claim: the four channels proved absent in EXP-031 will do most of the ruling out -- temporal order, ontological role, provenance, specificity
no domain will be wholly dead or wholly viable; the answer will be per-question
the questions that survive will mostly be 'are these two structures analogous' -- i.e. the thing EXP-048 already established -- rather than anything new
predictions.reason: if so, Stage 3 would be applying a known capability to new data rather than testing a new one, which is a weaker proposition and should be said plainly

predictions.claim: magnitude questions will now pass, having failed before EXP-034 added the weight channel
